# Render Pricing 2026: Total Cost & Competitors Compared

Author

Last updated

July 30, 2026

## [Copied to clipboardTL;DR](#tldr)

[Render](https://checkthat.ai/brands/render/) charges a flat workspace fee plus per-second compute. It adopted this $0 to $499/month workspace model on April 23, 2026, when it dropped per-seat charges and kept unlimited team members on paid tiers.

| Factor | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| Cost of Plans | $0 to $499/mo workspace fee (Enterprise is custom), plus per-second compute from $7/mo per web service and managed Postgres from $6/mo |
| Cost of Add-Ons | Postgres storage at $0.30/GB/mo, bandwidth overage at $0.15/GB, build minutes at $5 per 1,000 over quota, and a 20% HIPAA compute surcharge on Scale |
| Free Tier | Yes — Hobby workspaces cost $0 and include 750 free instance hours/month, but free web services spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity and free Postgres databases expire after 30 days |
| Vs. Competitors | Mixed — far cheaper than [Heroku](https://checkthat.ai/brands/heroku) for equivalent compute ($25 vs. $250 for a 2 GB-class service), but [Railway](https://checkthat.ai/brands/indian-railways), [Fly.io](https://checkthat.ai/brands/fly-io), and [DigitalOcean](https://checkthat.ai/brands/digitalocean) App Platform can undercut it on small or intermittent workloads |
| What Users Say | Mixed to negative — 2.6/5 on [Trustpilot](https://checkthat.ai/brands/trustpilot) from a small review pool; users praise the $7 Starter tier and savings over Heroku, but report surprise free-tier charges and objected to the April 2026 bandwidth cuts |

| Best for | Skip if |
| --- | --- |
| Teams of roughly 2–100 developers running standard web apps, especially those paying $250+/month on Heroku and wanting a similar deploy workflow at a fraction of the compute cost. | You need an always-on free tier, serve bandwidth-heavy traffic (overage runs $0.15/GB past small included quotas), want managed MySQL, or need fine-grained usage-based billing. |

## [Copied to clipboardRender Pricing](#render-pricing)

[Render](https://checkthat.ai/brands/render) pricing has two layers: a flat monthly [workspace fee](https://render.com/pricing) plus separate per-second compute charges. The workspace fee sets feature access, compliance certifications, and support level; compute covers every web service, worker, and database you run. The current plans took effect on [April 23, 2026](https://render.com/changelog/updated-plans-for-render-workspaces), when Render replaced its $19-per-member Professional plan with flat tiers and unlimited seats. Remaining legacy workspaces migrate automatically on August 1, 2026, and Render says [75% of paying customers](https://www.render.com/blog/better-pricing-for-fast-growing-teams) will see costs decrease or stay the same. Full [plan pricing details](https://checkthat.ai/brands/render/pricing/) break down as follows.

| Plan | Monthly | Included Bandwidth | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hobby | $0 | 5 GB/mo | Solo developers, prototypes, and learning projects (25 services max, vertical scaling only) |
| Pro | $25 | 25 GB/mo | Small production teams that need horizontal autoscaling, full-stack previews, and SOC 2 documentation |
| Scale | $499 | 1 TB/mo | Compliance-heavy teams needing HIPAA BAA, SAML SSO, SCIM, and organization audit logs |
| Enterprise | Custom pricing | Custom | Organizations requiring contractual uptime SLAs and a dedicated account manager |

## [Copied to clipboardRender Add-Ons](#render-add-ons)

The workspace fee is the floor, not the full bill, because it includes no compute. Anything you run is billed separately and prorated to the second:

* **Web services and background workers:** Instances run from Starter at $7/month (512 MB RAM, 0.5 CPU) through Standard at $25/month (2 GB, 1 CPU) up to Pro Ultra at $450/month (32 GB, 8 CPU), with custom instances up to 512 GB by sales quote.
* **Cron jobs and workflows:** Cron jobs bill per minute (from $0.00016/min on Starter) and Workflows, currently in beta, bill per hour with partial-hour proration from $0.05/hour to $7.00/hour.
* **PostgreSQL databases:** Paid instances range from Basic-256mb at $6/month to Pro-512gb at $6,200/month, with Accelerated instances reaching $11,000/month at 1 TB of RAM; the free tier expires 30 days after creation.
* **Postgres storage:** Database disk costs $0.30/GB per month, expandable in 5 GB increments that cannot be reduced later.
* **Redis (Key Value) stores:** Instances run from Starter at $10/month (256 MB) to Pro Ultra at $1,100/month (40 GB).
* **Persistent disks:** Block storage for self-managed databases ([MariaDB](https://checkthat.ai/brands/mariadb), [MongoDB](https://checkthat.ai/brands/mongodb), and similar) costs $0.25/GB per month.
* **Bandwidth overage:** Traffic beyond your plan's included quota bills at $0.15/GB, and Private Link outbound traffic bills separately at $0.03/GB on Pro and Scale.
* **Build pipeline overage:** Build minutes beyond plan quotas (500/month on Hobby, 1,000 on Pro, 5,000 on Scale) cost $5 per 1,000 minutes.
* **HIPAA compliance:** Running HIPAA workloads on Scale or Enterprise adds a [20% premium on compute spend](https://render.com/docs/hipaa-compliance), replacing the legacy $250/month minimum fee.

## [Copied to clipboardRender Total Cost of Ownership](#render-total-cost-of-ownership)

Because compute stacks on top of the workspace fee, two teams on the same $25 Pro plan can see very different bills. We modeled four common scenarios from Render's published rates:

| Scenario | What you pay for | Ballpark/month |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solo developer side project | Hobby workspace ($0) + Starter web service ($7) + Basic-256mb Postgres ($6) | $13 |
| 5-person production API team | Pro workspace ($25) + 2 Standard services ($50) + Pro-4gb Postgres ($55) + 20 GB Postgres storage ($6) | $135–$160 |
| 15-person SaaS with moderate traffic | Pro workspace ($25) + 2 Pro services ($170) + 1 Standard worker ($25) + Pro-8gb Postgres ($100) + Standard Redis ($32) + 100 GB storage ($30) + ~75 GB bandwidth overage (~$11) | $390–$450 |
| HIPAA healthcare startup | Scale workspace ($499) + 2 Standard services ($50) + Pro-4gb Postgres ($55) + 20% HIPAA surcharge on compute (~$21) | $625–$700 |

*Figures assume annual billing.*

## [Copied to clipboardWhat Reviews Say About Render Pricing](#what-reviews-say-about-render-pricing)

### [Copied to clipboardWhat People Tend to Like](#what-people-tend-to-like)

* **Cheap paid entry point:** Multiple Trustpilot reviewers describe the $7/month Starter instance as the fix for free-tier frustrations, delivering instant responses and simple [GitHub](https://checkthat.ai/brands/github)-linked deploys.
* **Real savings versus Heroku:** A self-taught Rails developer on [Reddit](https://checkthat.ai/brands/reddit) reported paying about $100/month for Render services after finding it the easiest platform to set up and manage.

### [Copied to clipboardWhat People Tend to Dislike](#what-people-tend-to-dislike)

* **Charges on "free" accounts:** Free instance hours running out only suspends services, but bandwidth overages generate [real charges on free tiers](https://community.render.com/t/confused-about-the-free-tier/19092), and several 1-star Trustpilot reviews from 2025–2026 report unexpected billing on free accounts.
* **The April 2026 bandwidth cut:** Included Pro bandwidth dropped from 500 GB to 25 GB (Hobby from 100 GB to 5 GB), and a [Hacker News commenter](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48235993) called the change "a major price hike for indie developers."
* **Compute surprises on paid plans:** A community forum user assumed the workspace plan covered compute until Render staff clarified that "compute costs are always additional to the plan cost."
* **Arrears billing after cancellation:** Because Render always bills in arrears, users who suspend or close accounts mid-month still receive charges for prior usage, which several Trustpilot reviewers read as deceptive.
* **Costs climb at production scale:** Prateek J., a DevSecOps architect, wrote in a [4.5-star G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/render-render/reviews) that "Pricing becomes less competitive as workloads grow" once you run multiple services, workers, and databases at production tiers.

### [Copied to clipboardExample Reviews](#example-reviews)

For $7.00 a month, you get instant responses, it is super easy to set up an api, and then, super simple to keep it updated by linking a GitHub repository. Fantastic!" — Nick Chater

> "Free tier is garbage. Server goes to sleep within hours and you can't access what you worked on. I upgraded to their paid services, and I haven't had a problem since. The people that are complaining need to quit being cheap and spent the $7 a month." — Bobby Beam

> "they charged me on my free tier account for nothing, if i need to pay why the hell would i go for free tier" — Muhammad Naveed

| [Engine Yard](https://checkthat.ai/brands/engine-yard/) | [$270/mo platform fee](https://www.engineyard.com/pricing/) | No (14-day trial) | About $339+ | High-touch managed support for Ruby, PHP, Node.js, Java, or Python on your own AWS EC2 |

### [Copied to clipboardRender vs Heroku](#render-vs-heroku)

Choose Render when cost drives the decision: a [2 GB Render service](https://render.com/docs/render-vs-heroku-comparison) runs $25/month against $250/month for Heroku's 2.5 GB Performance-M dyno, and Render offers up to $10K in migration credits plus hands-on migration help. Stay on Heroku if your team depends on its add-on ecosystem or runs very high-traffic workloads, since one 2,800 RPS migration reported its bill jumping from about $700/month on Heroku to about $4,500/month on Render.

### [Copied to clipboardRender vs Railway](#render-vs-railway)

Choose Render for flat, forecastable fees, a permanent free workspace, and a Heroku-style dashboard experience. Choose Railway when per-second billing on the $1/month Hobby plan fits an intermittent workload, since third-party estimates put a small app with a bundled database at $5–$10/month, well under a comparable Render stack.

### [Copied to clipboardRender vs Fly.io](#render-vs-flyio)

Choose Render if you want tiered instance pricing you can budget in advance and a simpler onboarding path for teams that live in the dashboard. Choose Fly.io for globally distributed apps, where egress in North America and Europe costs $0.02/GB and the pure pay-as-you-go model rewards teams comfortable optimizing from the CLI.

### [Copied to clipboardRender vs DigitalOcean App Platform](#render-vs-digitalocean-app-platform)

Choose Render for a broader set of integrated managed services, including Postgres, Redis, cron jobs, and workflows, under one billing model. Choose DigitalOcean App Platform if you want a small production app for about $32/month, a free static-site tier, or tight integration with existing DigitalOcean infrastructure; that $32 estimate combines a $25 container with a $7 development database.

### [Copied to clipboardRender vs Engine Yard](#render-vs-engine-yard)

Choose Render if you want a self-serve platform where a small production stack costs a fraction of Engine Yard's $270/month Standard platform fee before EC2 instance costs even start. Choose Engine Yard if you want 12×5 or 24×7 managed support running your Ruby, PHP, Node.js, Java, or Python workloads on AWS and are willing to pay roughly $339+/month for the hand-holding.

## [Copied to clipboardIs Render's Pricing Worth It?](#is-renders-pricing-worth-it)

Render's pricing is worthwhile when:

* **You pay $250+/month on Heroku:** Equivalent Render compute costs a fraction of Heroku dyno pricing, and third-party analysis found a standard SaaS stack at $138/month on Render versus $350/month on Heroku.
* **Your team has multiple developers:** The flat $25/month Pro plan with unlimited seats beats the legacy $19-per-member model for any team of two or more.
* **You want managed infrastructure without a DevOps hire:** Managed Postgres with point-in-time recovery, Redis, cron jobs, autoscaling, and preview environments all live on one platform.
* **Your traffic is steady and bandwidth-light:** Apps staying under Pro's 25 GB monthly bandwidth quota avoid the $0.15/GB overage entirely, keeping bills close to sticker price.

Choose another platform when:

* **You need an always-on free tier:** Free Render services spin down after [15 minutes without traffic](https://render.com/docs/free) and take about a minute to wake, and free Postgres databases expire after 30 days.
* **Your app serves heavy bandwidth:** At $0.15/GB past 25 GB on Pro, media-heavy or high-egress apps accumulate overage far faster than on Fly.io ($0.02/GB in North America and Europe) or Railway ($0.05/GB).
* **You run very high-traffic workloads:** The 2,800 RPS Judoscale migration is a documented case of Render costing several times more than Heroku at scale.
* **You want usage-based granularity:** Railway and Fly.io bill active resource consumption by the second with no flat workspace fee, which suits spiky or experimental workloads better.
